evals.prompt: I'm implementing a ProductCard organism. On mobile (< 360px) it should show a compact vertical layout, and on larger screens it should show the standard horizontal layout. How do I implement this?
evals.expected_output: Uses LayoutBuilder with constraints.maxWidth < 360 breakpoint. Delegates to _buildCompact() and _buildDefault(). Explains that organisms should ALWAYS consider responsiveness. Uses ConstrainedBox for max widths instead of hardcoded SizedBox.

assertions.text: Response uses LayoutBuilder with constraints.maxWidth to detect breakpoints
Response uses < 360px as the compact breakpoint
Response states organisms should ALWAYS consider responsiveness

evals.prompt: I have a horizontal Row with a product title Text on the left and a price badge on the right. On compact screens I'm getting overflow errors. How do I fix it without changing the Figma text?
evals.expected_output: Wraps title in Flexible or Expanded. Explicitly states TextOverflow.ellipsis only when Figma defines truncation. Never shorten, translate, or rewrite Figma text. Layout adapts, text is preserved.

assertions.text: Response wraps the title Text in Flexible or Expanded to allow shrinking
Response explicitly states that TextOverflow.ellipsis should only be used when Figma or the technical contract defines truncation
Response states that Figma literal text must NOT be shortened to avoid overflow — layout adapts instead

evals.prompt: I'm implementing a DS ProductCard for both mobile and desktop. What are the correct max widths to use for each platform, and what pattern should I use to switch between them?
evals.expected_output: Mobile max width: 327px, desktop max width: 610px. Uses platform parameter (TargetPlatform) and ConstrainedBox with BoxConstraints. Never hardcodes SizedBox with fixed width in production widgets (only in golden tests).

assertions.text: Response uses 327px for mobile and 610px for desktop max widths
Response uses ConstrainedBox with BoxConstraints to apply max widths
Response warns against hardcoding fixed widths in production widgets (only acceptable in golden tests)
